analysis: All 14 supplied units are test-only changes: StatusResidencyTests.swift (adds two CLI status tests, lines 119-176), AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift (two new test-only ProviderLoop setters, lines 120-126), and three added test files (SelectedModelPlacementPolicyTests, SelectedModelRecoveryFixture, SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests). No production source is modified, so no change to the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002), attestation, App Attest (TB-011), key custody, the prefix cache (T-041) or the fan helper. The new setters sit in the test target behind @testable import and do not widen the production attack surface. The tests describe policy that the production code must implement. A selected model outranks an expired Autopilot placement. Holds are always honored (the aHeldAdoptionIsNeverReleased test). An add-on hold cancels an in-progress recovery load (TB-012/T-059, anAddonHoldCancelsTheAttemptInProgress). A live Autopilot lease and other residency owners pause recovery. The supplied evidence does not include the production implementation, so these behaviors are unverified here. The production selected-model recovery code, which evicts or releases adopted models, and its interaction with add-on holds (T-059) and with request-in-flight handling should be examined in whichever review pass covers those source files. The status tests only write synthetic daemon-state JSON into a temporary sandbox and use fake model IDs and hashes. They contain no secrets and no real network or keychain access. The tests leak nothing and reveal no regression.
